summary: Lawrence County secondary fire tower reported in 1940, with a cab enclosure planned in 1942; listed as gone, and no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Open platform, 'Crow's Nest' type, with a cab enclosure planned in 1942
facts.status_note: Listed as gone; no source describes what, if anything, remains at the site

events.note: Reported in September 1940 as about to be established; completion is not confirmed in the sources read
Homer Lloyd named local resident watchman

evidence.supports: 1940 secondary tower to be established with Homer Lloyd as local watchman
evidence.quote: A secondary fire tower is to be established on Telegraph hill four miles south of Blackfork with Homer Lloyd as local resident watchman.

evidence.supports: open platform crow's nest type, no protection from the elements
evidence.quote: They are the open platform or 'Crow's Nest ' type and give no protection from the elements to the towermen.

evidence.supports: two cab enclosures received by the Forest Service
evidence.quote: Two fire tower cabin enclosures have been received by the U.S. Forest Service.

evidence.supports: cab to be installed on the Telegraph Hill tower a mile east of State Route 75
evidence.quote: They will be installed on the Telegraph Hill tower a mile east of state route 75 on Telegraph hill.

evidence.supports: Carl Malone manned the tower in 1942
evidence.quote: The tower is manned by Carl Malone.

evidence.supports: CCC from Camp Vesuvius to do the construction
evidence.quote: The construction will be done by CCC from Camp Vesuvius under the direction of Engineer Foreman Joseph Swisher.

evidence.supports: cabs to protect equipment and keep people from gaining access
evidence.quote: prevent persons from gaining access to the towers

evidence.supports: government ruling barred the general public from climbing; towers in use as airplane spotter stations and for other war work
evidence.quote: a recent ruling of the government prohibits climbing of the towers by the general public

evidence.supports: secondary towers manned only when fire hazard is high
evidence.quote: These two are known as secondary towers and are manned only when the fire hazard is high.

evidence.supports: Ohio list marks the tower as gone
evidence.quote: Telegraph Hill Lawrence 38.78222 -82.59001 Tower Gone FFLOS US 1573, OH 19

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts entry ends with the word Removed, no date given
register places the site in Wayne National Forest
register lists the U.S. Forest Service as the agency

notes_for_editor: The 1940 item says a secondary tower was to be established, so the built event is a planned date; completion is not confirmed. The 1942 item uses future tense for the cab installation, which is not confirmed as completed. Record agency and ownership fit the sources. No source found on the removal date or the site today. A search snippet (not read, not used) says a Shawnee tower is the last Wayne National Forest tower; it is secondary and unverified.
